summary: Frontend-only regression pass for the two internal perf refactors (engine.js getSnapshot() mutate-in-place, DrunkPigeon.js pushTimer() self-untracking one-shot timers). Verified via Playwright at 412x915: main menu loads, all 4 maps (Sunny London/Gritty Backstreets/Chippy Sunset/Random) launch gameplay with game-pigeon rendering, distance-hud/chip-hud update correctly, collision -> game-over-overlay shows correct final DISTANCE and CHIPS EATEN (verifies snapshot data is not stale/corrupted). Ran 8/8 consecutive Game Over -> Play Again cycles: each new run began with a clean scene (obstacle/chip DOM counts consistent, no ghosted leftover entities from previous runs bleeding into the fresh engine.reset()). Ran a sustained ~60s continuous session with 113 flap taps interleaved with restart-on-death, then triggered revive flow: revive-button granted revive (web mock AdMob), gameplay resumed with pigeon visible; the second game-over of the same session correctly hid revive-button (one-time gating intact). Zero console errors and zero pageerrors observed across the entire session.

code_review_of_refactor.engine_js_getSnapshot: Correct. outObs/outChips/outFeathers arrays pre-allocated ONCE to match obstacles/chips/feathers pool sizes; each frame the for-loop mutates each element's fields (x, y, active, anim, eaten, rot, life). outHeckler/outJab/outPint are singleton objects mutated in place. Top-level returned wrapper object is still a fresh literal each call (required for Reanimated shared-value !== check to fire). Inactive slots correctly reflect out.active=0 - GameEntities.js worklet consumers gate rendering on .active so no ghost visuals possible.
code_review_of_refactor.DrunkPigeon_pushTimer: Correct. untrack(id) uses indexOf + splice to remove the timer id from timers.current the instant the callback fires. Bulk-clear on unmount still walks timers.current and clearTimeout()s remaining ids, so cancellation semantics are unchanged. setInterval-based ambient bubble loop uses its own ref and is untouched, as documented in the code comment.

critical_code_review_comments: getSnapshot() correctly returns a fresh top-level object every frame to satisfy Reanimated's referential-equality change detection while reusing the child containers - the design intent is well-documented in the source comment and is functionally correct.

The self-untracking timer helper in DrunkPigeon.js is a strict improvement over the previous unbounded-growth pattern; no functional cadence/timing change to random-event scheduler was observed during testing.
No regressions found in this pass; refactor is safe to ship for the perf-motivated goal.
seed_data_creation: localStorage.clear() at test start to guarantee fresh best-score baseline
context_for_next_testing_agent: Refactor regression verified functionally. Correct testids reused from iteration_34: play-button, map-day/night/dusk/random, game-pigeon, distance-hud, chip-hud, game-over-overlay, go-distance, go-chips, go-best-distance, play-again-button, revive-button, menu-button. Web preview mocks AdMob so revive always grants reward - one-time gating is enforced at UI level in GameOverOverlay and is confirmed working (2nd death in same session hides revive-button).
limitations: CRITICAL LIMITATION: Real-device frame pacing / FPS (60/90/120Hz) and micro-stutter measurement on low-end Android is NOT possible in this Playwright/web-preview environment. This report verifies only functional and visual-correctness regression of the two refactors (no stale/ghosted data, no memory-growth symptoms in a ~60s session, no console errors, revive/restart/collision/game-over flows intact). It DOES NOT and cannot confirm that the actual micro-stutter perceived on the Android APK is resolved - that requires on-device profiling (systrace/perfetto or in-app frame-time logging) which must be validated by the user on real hardware.
